stories.headline: ‘Thank You, Colombia’: James Rodríguez retires after an extraordinary 15 years
stories.deck: James Rodríguez has retired from international football after 15 years and 131 appearances for Colombia. The iconic No. 10 leaves as the country’s record cap holder, with 31 goals and 43 assists. His career was defined by the 2014 World Cup Golden Boot and memorable performances. At 35, Rodríguez will continue his club career with Atlético Nacional.
stories.bodyText:
For 15 years, James Rodríguez was one of the first names that came to mind whenever Colombia walked onto a football pitch. The No. 10 shirt became closely associated with him, as did the captain’s armband, the spectacular goals and the expectations that followed him through three World Cups. On Tuesday, Rodríguez announced his international retirement in an emotional video, telling Colombian fans that it was time to close “one of the most important chapters” of his life. After 131 appearances for his country, the legendary No. 10 has brought that chapter to an end.
From a winning debut to Colombia's record cap holder
Rodríguez's international story began in October 2011, when he made his Colombia debut against Bolivia and immediately announced himself by scoring the winning goal.
He was only beginning what would become a 15-year relationship with the national team, eventually playing at the 2014, 2018 and 2026 World Cups. Colombia did not qualify for the 2022 tournament in Qatar, meaning Rodríguez's international career ultimately spanned three editions of football's biggest competition despite the four-year absence. He is tied with Carlos Valderrama and Freddy Rincon for the most tournament appearances by a Colombian.
The tournament that defined his reputation, however, came in Brazil in 2014.
Rodríguez scored six goals in five matches to win the World Cup Golden Boot, including the extraordinary volley against Uruguay in the last 16 that became one of the defining goals of the tournament and later won the FIFA Puskás Award.
Colombia reached the quarter-finals before losing to hosts Brazil, but Rodríguez's performances had already changed the trajectory of his career. After the tournament, he earned his move from Monaco to Real Madrid, where he would play alongside some of the biggest names in world football.
For Colombia, meanwhile, the No. 10 had become much more than a shirt number.
Rodríguez eventually took on the responsibility of captaining his country as well, carrying the armband during a period in which Colombia remained one of South America's strongest sides.
He finished his international career as Colombia's record cap holder, level with Carlos Valderrama and Freddy Rincón for the most tournament appearances by a Colombian, while his final figures stood at 131 appearances, 31 goals and 43 assists.
The captaincy, the tears and one more World Cup
Rodríguez's relationship with Colombia was never defined solely by the highlights.
In his retirement message, he acknowledged the difficult periods alongside the celebrations and explained what representing the national team had meant to him throughout his career.
“Today, I want to talk to you from the heart,” James said on social media on Tuesday. “After many years, many games and joys, and difficult moments, it's time to close one of the most important chapters in my life: my journey with the Colombian national team.”
He described the responsibility attached to the shirt in equally personal terms.
“Wearing this shirt was a dream, but also a huge responsibility,” James added. “Every time I entered a court, I understood that he didn't play just for me. I played for my family, teammates, thousands of Colombians who dreamed of all of us.
“I had the honor of wearing the No. 10 shirt and also the captain's armband. I always tried to do it with respect, responsibility and understanding what it meant to represent Colombia. I had good days and very difficult ones, but I never stopped feeling proud of these colors.”
His final appearance came on July 7, when Colombia faced Switzerland in the last 16 of the 2026 World Cup.
The match finished 0-0 after extra time, before Switzerland won the penalty shootout 4-3, bringing Rodríguez's fourth and final World Cup campaign to an end.
It also meant his last match for Colombia ended without the fairytale finish that might have suited the player who had given the country one of its most memorable individual World Cup performances.
There had been another significant chapter two years earlier.
Rodríguez captained Colombia to the 2024 Copa América final, where Argentina won 1-0 after extra time. It was Colombia's first appearance in the Copa América title match in 23 years, although Rodríguez ultimately finished his international career without a senior international trophy.
Why James Rodríguez decided to walk away
His announcement was direct, with Rodríguez making clear that his decision was not about distancing himself from Colombia but about bringing an important period of his life to a natural conclusion.
The caption accompanying his retirement video said: “Thank you for every match, every joy, every tear and every dream we shared. Defending the colours of the Colombia national team was one of the greatest honours of my life.”
He ended the message with the same sense of gratitude.
“I'm leaving calmly because I gave everything. Thank you for every moment, thank you Colombia,” Rodríguez said.
Rodríguez is now 
35
, and while his international career is finished, he has made clear that he is not finished with football.
Rodríguez's club career continues in Colombia
Just last week, Rodríguez joined Atlético Nacional on a contract running through next June after leaving Minnesota United.
The move takes him back to Colombian football for the first time since his teenage years at Envigado, where his professional career began, and gives the veteran midfielder an opportunity to continue playing in his home country after closing the door on international football.
Atlético Nacional becomes the 14th club of a career that has taken Rodríguez through some of the biggest teams in Europe and North America, including Real Madrid, Bayern Munich and Everton.
His club honours include two Champions League titles and two LaLiga crowns, while his international career produced the Golden Boot at the 2014 World Cup, 31 goals, 43 assists and more appearances for Colombia than any other player.
There will be no more World Cup nights in the yellow shirt, no further Copa América campaigns and no additional occasions for Rodríguez to walk out wearing Colombia's No. 10 or captain's armband.
For a generation of Colombian supporters, those two symbols had become inseparable from the same player.
Now Rodríguez will try to write the final pages of his playing career at Atlético Nacional, while the Colombia team begins the task of imagining its midfield and its No. 10 shirt without the player who occupied both for so long.

stories.headline: Messi set for Argentina farewell in Benin friendly
stories.deck: The October 6 match will serve as his farewell appearance after announcing his international retirement last month.
stories.bodyText:
Lionel Messi was on Tuesday (September 15, 2026) named in Argentina's squad for a friendly against Benin on October 6, a match that will serve as his farewell appearance after announcing his international retirement last month.
The 39-year-old said in August he was retiring from Argentina duty after a two-decade international career that included winning the 2022 World Cup and Copa America triumphs in 2021 and 2024.
"We made the decision to invite the best player in the world, the symbol of our national team, our captain, Lionel Andres Messi, so that he can have the farewell he truly deserves on October 6 here in Argentina," said Argentine FA president Claudio Tapia.
The match against Benin will take place at River Plate's Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires, which can accommodate 85,000 spectators.
Tapia also invited all of Argentina's 2022 World Cup winners to join Messi for what he said would be an "unforgettable" occasion.
Argentina begin a series of three friendlies against Bolivia on September 30 in Cordoba — their first match since losing the World Cup final to Spain — before taking on Burkina Faso in Buenos Aires on October 3.
Messi has been included in the squad for the third match against Benin, when he is expected to make his 208th and final appearance for the national team. He is Argentina's all-time record scorer with 125 goals.
Following the death of his father Jorge last month, Messi had said he had "serious doubts" about continuing to play football of any sort for "much longer". "It was a decision that hurt and still hurts deep in my soul but I understand that it is the right time," Messi said when he called time on his Argentina career.
His contract with Major League Soccer club Inter Miami runs until the end of the 2028 season.
Last month FIFA ordered Argentina to play their next home match with capacity reduced to 50 percent for breaches of its disciplinary code relating to using a sports event for making demonstrations of a non-sporting nature.
After Argentina beat England 2-1 in a tense World Cup semi-final in July, several players held up a banner saying: "The Falklands are Argentine".
The friendlies are also expected to count towards suspensions handed down following incidents after Argentina's World Cup final defeat by Spain.
Midfielder Leandro Paredes received a 10-match ban, while defender Nahuel Molina was suspended for seven games and Thiago Almada for one.

briefs.headline: India-Afghanistan 2nd T20I: Nitish, Samson to the fore as Men in Blue seal series with ease
briefs.deck: The medium-pacer’s career-best figures helps India restrict Afghanistan to 159 for eight; the opener roars back with a 22-ball 57 while Abhishek, too, fires in the modest chase
briefs.bodyText:
In the quest for a seam-bowling all-rounder, particularly when Hardik Pandya’s battle with injuries has resembled a long-running soap opera, India has backed Nitish Kumar for the best part of two years. The 23-year-old from Visakhapatnam has himself had his tryst with injuries of late, but evenings like the one at the Arun Jaitley Stadium on Tuesday will go a long way towards boosting the youngster’s confidence.
Nitish, who has ramped up his speed in recent months, scalped three for 24 in his three overs as Shreyas Iyer & Co. restricted Afghanistan to 159 for eight and clinched a seven-wicket win in 14.5 overs. With it, India took an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match T20I series.
After conceding 30 runs in two overs in Sunday’s (September 13, 2026) opener, Nitish needed a productive outing with the ball, especially as he was returning from a quadriceps injury.
If Nitish stepped up, so did Sanju Samson. With 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi watching from the dugout in the first two games, the pressure on the 31-year-old to hold his own as opener is unmistakable in every outing. In the circumstances, Samson responded ably with a belligerent 22-ball 57.
Once again, Jasprit Bumrah set the foundation by starting with a maiden over. Arshdeep Singh reaped the rewards in the next over. Off the left-armer’s third delivery, Rahmanullah Gurbaz’s desperation to get Afghanistan off the mark manifested in a hasty pull. The miscue was pouched by Ravi Bishnoi at mid-on.
After the second-wicket stand between Ibrahim Zadran and Sediqullah Atal accrued 51 runs, Nitish delivered the breakthrough as the Afghan skipper’s heave across the line found deep midwicket.
Bishnoi, who replaced the injured Varun Chakaravarthy, struck shortly after when Sediquulah holed out to Tilak Varma at long-off. More joy came India’s way as Gulbadin Naib skied Nitish to Samson.
A brisk 29-run stand between Azmatullah Omarzai and Darwish Rasooli was laced with lusty blows. Omarzai even had that tincture of luck that every batter needs when Bishnoi spilled an easy chance off Axar Patel’s left-arm spin with the Afghan all-rounder on five. But when both batters departed in quick succession, the Afghans were back in a blind alley at 100 for six in 14.1 overs.
In getting to the total that Zadran & Co. ultimately did, Mohammad Nabi and Rashid Khan displayed their secondary skills. The spin duo, more than capable of chipping in with the willow, put together 48 runs for the seventh wicket.
Will such cameos suffice, however, against this Indian unit? Not on Tuesday’s (September 15) evidence.

briefs.headline: Ronaldo suffers worst Al-Nassr defeat to date in 4-0 Champions League loss
briefs.deck: Cristiano Ronaldo and Al-Nassr endured a nightmare return to the AFC Champions League Elite, suffering a 4-0 defeat to Al-Ain. The result marks Ronaldo’s heaviest loss since joining the Saudi club in 2023 and leaves Al-Nassr bottom after Matchday 1. Ange Postecoglou’s side now face seven remaining league-stage matches to recover from their disastrous opening.
briefs.bodyText:
Al-Nassr's return to the AFC Champions League Elite was supposed to offer an early glimpse of what the new season could bring. Instead, 
Cristiano Ronaldo
 and his teammates walked away from their opening night with a result that few inside the club would have expected, as Ange Postecoglou's side suffered a heavy defeat in the United Arab Emirates.
Al-Nassr suffer nightmare start against Al-Ain
Cristiano Ronaldo started for Al-Nassr, but there was little the captain could do to prevent a disastrous evening as Al-Ain swept aside the Saudi side 4-0 in their first AFC Champions League Elite match of the campaign.
The defeat came in Matchday 1 of the newly formatted competition, meaning Al-Nassr's Asian campaign has barely begun, but the manner of the loss immediately puts Postecoglou's team under pressure.
Al-Ain took control in the 25th minute, when Houssine Rahimi opened the scoring. Al-Nassr were unable to find a response before Rahimi struck again in the 63rd minute, leaving the visitors with a huge task just to get back into the match.
Instead, the collapse continued.
Soufiane Rahimi added a third in the 72nd minute, before Georgios Giakoumakis completed the rout five minutes from full-time to seal a stunning 4-0 victory for the UAE side.
For all of Al-Nassr's possession, there was remarkably little attacking threat to show for it. Postecoglou's team controlled 58 per cent of possession and won the corner count 10-2, yet managed only three shots on target.
Al-Ain, by comparison, registered seven shots on target and made their opportunities count.
The result also extends an impressive start to the season for Al-Ain, who arrived unbeaten in their first five UAE Pro League matches, having recorded four wins and one draw.
Ronaldo suffers heaviest Al-Nassr defeat
For Ronaldo, the scale of the defeat makes it particularly difficult to dismiss as an ordinary bad night.
It is now the heaviest defeat of his Al-Nassr career since he joined the Saudi club in January 2023. His previous worst results in Saudi colours had both ended in three-goal defeats, with Al-Nassr losing 3-0 to Al-Hilal in the Saudi Pro League in December 2023 and 4-1 to the same opponents in the Saudi Super Cup in August 2024.
The 4-0 defeat to Al-Ain is therefore a new low in terms of the margin of defeat during Ronaldo's time in 
Saudi Arabia
.
It does not, however, match the heaviest losses of his entire career. Ronaldo's two worst defeats by goal difference remain Manchester United's 5-0 loss to Liverpool in October 2021 and Real Madrid's 5-0 defeat to Barcelona in November 2010, both five-goal margins.
What makes Tuesday's result particularly damaging is when it arrived.
Al-Nassr had only just returned to the AFC Champions League Elite after a one-year gap, with a new coach, a new season and renewed expectations surrounding a squad built to compete for major honours.
The opening match was supposed to begin that campaign.
Instead, Al-Nassr now sit at the bottom of the tournament standings after one match, having conceded four goals without scoring.
Al-Nassr have seven matches to repair the damage
The new AFC Champions League Elite format gives Al-Nassr some room to recover because this is no longer a traditional four-team group containing six matches.
Instead, the competition now features a single league stage in which each team plays eight matches against eight different opponents.
That means Al-Nassr have seven matchdays remaining, giving Ronaldo and his teammates plenty of opportunities to climb the table after their disastrous opening.
Their next opportunity comes on October 12, when Al-Nassr host FK Neftchi Fergana.
The scale of the response will matter as much as the result itself. A one-year absence from the competition had created anticipation around Al-Nassr's return, while Postecoglou had arrived with the task of turning a squad containing Ronaldo and other high-profile additions into a side capable of making a serious continental run.
Instead, the first night exposed just how far there is still to go.
Al-Nassr fans turn on Ronaldo and Postecoglou
The reaction from the stands was predictably furious after Al-Nassr were beaten at the Hazza bin Zayed Stadium.
Supporters had expected something very different from the club's return to Asia's elite competition, particularly with Ronaldo leading the side and Postecoglou now in charge.
Some fans directed their anger towards Ronaldo himself, with the captain's performance described by supporters as “pitiful” amid Al-Nassr's failure to seriously threaten Al-Ain for long periods.
Postecoglou faced even sharper criticism.
Supporters questioned whether the Australian had made the difference they expected after his appointment, with Al-Nassr appearing short of answers at both ends of the pitch as the scoreline continued to worsen.
Calls for his dismissal grew louder as the defeat unfolded.
For a club that entered its AFC Champions League Elite return with ambitions of going deep into the competition, there could hardly have been a more damaging opening night. Ronaldo and Al-Nassr now have seven matches to change the story, but the first one has already left them with a four-goal deficit and very little margin for another collapse.

briefs.headline: Asian Games 2026: J&K govt. allows Mir Bilquis to travel after SC intervention; to coach Indian kayaking, canoeing team
briefs.deck: The Supreme Court on September 10 issued an order in favour of the sportsperson and quashed an official order denying her permission, citing pending departmental inquiries and service conditions.
briefs.bodyText:
In line with recent directions by the Supreme Court, the Jammu and Kashmir government on Tuesday (September 15, 2026) granted permission to Bilquis Mir, a Physical Education Teacher, to discharge her duties as the chief coach of the Indian National Kayaking and Canoeing team for the Asian Games in Japan.
“Ms. Mir, Physical Education Teacher, is hereby accorded the requisite limited No Objection Certificate (NOC)/permission and is relieved for the purpose of joining and discharging the remaining assignment as Coach/Chief Coach of the Indian National Kayaking and Canoeing Team and for accompanying and assisting the Indian National Team in connection with the Asian Games, 2026,” read the order, issued by the Department of Youth Services and Sports.
However, the official order said the permission shall remain “operative only for the period reasonably necessary for completion of the Asian Games 2026 assignment and connected official travel”.
“No permission is granted under this order for any private foreign travel or for any travel or engagement unconnected with the national sporting assignment covered by the judgment of the Hon’ble Supreme Court,” it added.
Ms. Mir has missed two international events since 2023 due to the denial of travel permission. “I urge all to support sportspersons of J&K. I am happy to the represent India and will serve my country,” Ms. Mir said.
The Supreme Court on September 10 issued an order in favour of Ms. Mir and quashed an official order denying her permission, citing pending departmental inquiries and service conditions.
ACB inquiry in 2023
In 2023, Ms. Mir faced an Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) inquiry over an anonymous complaint, questioning whether she possessed a Bachelor in Physical Education course to become a Physical Education Teacher (PET) or not.
In July 2025, the J&K High Court quashed the First Information Report (FIR) and described the investigation agency’s role as a “witch-hunt”.
Justice Sanjay Dhar of the J&K High Court, who passed the order quashing the FIR, observed that the attitude of the investigating agency “in criminalizing non-acquisition of a technical qualification by the petitioner when she has brought laurels to the country all over the world speaks volumes about the manner in which we are treating our sporting heroes”.
She became the first Indian woman on the Paris Olympics jury in 2024 and acted as the Chief Finish Line Judge at the 2025 Asian Championship held in Nanjing, China.
Ms. Mir, who once served as the secretary of the J&K Water Sports Kayaking and Canoeing Association, earned her the sobriquet of ‘Aqua Queen’ of Kashmir for training local boys and girls in different water sports since 1998.

briefs.headline: Stability at the top: On the tennis and the U.S. Open
briefs.deck: Both men’s and women’s tennis now wear a settled look
briefs.bodyText:
In recent times, men’s tennis has had a heavy dose of predictability while the women’s game has been in a state of perpetual flux. If Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner cornered 11 of the 13 Majors starting Wimbledon 2023, there were nine different winners among women in the same period. But at the recently concluded U.S. Open, this pattern flipped. Alexander Zverev won his second men’s singles Slam trophy and first at Flushing Meadows after finishing atop an airy field that lost Sinner before the tournament and Alcaraz in the quarterfinal. In the ladies category, Elena Rybakina secured her third Major — also her first in New York — after beating top seed and two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka, and No. 4 and 2023 U.S. Open winner Coco Gauff, back to back. Among the last four of Zverev, Ben Shelton, Frances Tiafoe and Karen Khachanov, the tall German was the only one with Slam-winning experience, having grabbed his maiden top prize at the 2026 French Open, a similarly open competition where Alcaraz was missing and Sinner exited early. On the other hand, the WTA top-four reached the semifinals, and it was only fitting that Rybakina’s splendid run ended with her being crowned the new World No. 1, ending Sabalenka’s reign of 99 straight weeks at the pinnacle.
The absence of a strong field, however, should not diminish Zverev’s accomplishment. While it is true that the 29-year-old faced just one top-10 opponent — Shelton in the final on Sunday — across his two triumphs at Roland-Garros and the U.S. Open, he is indisputably among the three best players in the world along with Alcaraz and Sinner. Sandwiched between his two title successes was a Wimbledon final appearance, where he fought Sinner tooth and nail. In fact, Zverev’s ascent reinforces the idea of a new Big Three in men’s tennis, and has neatly coincided with 24-time Major winner Novak Djokovic losing in the first round and tumbling out of the ATP top 10. For the first time since the early 2000s, none of Roger Federer, Rafael Nadal and Djokovic — the previous era’s Big Three — is ranked in the top 10, and the setback leaves the 39-year-old Serbian great facing an existential threat. Sabalenka, despite being a worthy runner-up to Rybakina, would have also left the U.S. with more questions than answers. The 28-year-old Belarusian has lost four of her last five Slam finals, and all of them as World No. 1, calling into question her big-match temperament. Worryingly, she only has a 50% success rate in all finals while being the top-ranked woman (7-7), an anomaly that requires a quick correction.

briefs.headline: Ruthless Rybakina dethrones Sabalenka to claim first U.S. Open crown
briefs.deck: An ankle injury had threatened to derail Rybakina's ‌campaign even before the tournament started, but the 27-year-old shrugged ‌off ⁠those concerns to add the U.S. Open title ⁠to her Australian Open triumph this year
briefs.bodyText:
Elena Rybakina delivered a devastating performance to dethrone two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka with a 6-4 5-7 6-2 win in the U.S. Open final on Saturday (September 12, 2026), earning a third Grand Slam crown to accompany her ascent to world number one.
The Russian-born Kazakh's icy composure on the grand stage helped her snap Sabalenka's 20-match winning streak at Flushing Meadows and denied the Belarusian the chance to emulate Serena Williams and Chris Evert with three straight New York titles.
An ankle injury had threatened to derail Rybakina's campaign even before the tournament started, but the 27-year-old shrugged off those concerns to add the U.S. Open title to her Australian Open triumph this year and Wimbledon success in 2022.
Saturday's title showdown at Arthur Ashe Stadium had all the ingredients of a classic between the top two in the rankings and though Sabalenka brought late aggression, Rybakina was typically unruffled and prevailed to pocket the $5.5 million prize.
Dressed in a yellow-and-black outfit that evoked a bee, Rybakina produced some stinging groundstrokes but was unable to make the early pressure count as Sabalenka unleashed big serves to hold firm in the pair's third Grand Slam final meeting.
The second seed drew first blood to go ahead 3-2 following a Sabalenka double fault, with the frustrated Belarusian earning a code violation immediately afterwards for launching a ball high into the stands of the main showcourt.
Sabalenka's irritation became increasingly evident with each missed shot and squandered opportunity, in stark contrast to the trademark calm etched on Rybakina's face as the Kazakh tightened her grip on the opening set and clinched it with a tight hold.
A sudden drop-off in Rybakina's level midway through the second set gave the 28-year-old Sabalenka hope, and she produced a delicate drop shot and a stunning backhand crosscourt winner en route to forcing a deciding set.
Sabalenka let out a huge roar after another backhand winner to hold in a tight opening game of the third set.
However, Rybakina's quality shone through her red-and-blue-framed racket as she took a commanding 5-2 lead and then closed out a famous triumph to leave her Belarusian rival without any major silverware in 2026.

briefs.headline: Indian team’s defence needs to display more coordination: Sreejesh
briefs.deck: While the Asian Games come with Olympic qualification on the line, the legendary goalkeeper believes bigger pressures loom in the Qualifier pathway
briefs.bodyText:
The gap between India’s World Cup exit and the opening whistle at the Asian Games — close to four weeks — gives the players and coaches barely enough time to catch their breath, let alone rebuild completely.
And former captain and goalkeeper P.R. Sreejesh, who believes that Indian hockey is not broken but rather stuck in a loop of avoidable mistakes, attributed the men’s team’s recurring defensive lapses to structural gaps.
“When we used to play, we used to go for more man-to-man marking... Nowadays we’re playing a system which is very deep and different, which needs more communication and understanding, because you may see two or three people in the same zone, and sometimes you get confused about whom you should go and mark,” he explained in a virtual interaction.
It’s a tactical shift that demands a level of coordination the team hasn’t fully mastered, especially against opponents who thrive on individual skill and interchange running.
While the Asian Games come with Olympic qualification on the line, Sreejesh believes bigger pressures loom in the Qualifier pathway.
He cited 2018 as evidence, when India missed out on a direct Olympic berth but found its way to the 2020 Tokyo Games through the qualifiers, and came home with a bronze medal. In the news regularly now for his frank assessments of the ecosystem, Sreejesh underlines that his intention was never to criticise anyone.
“This is my team. If I don’t tell my players it’s time to wake up, who is going to?” he asked.
The 38-year-old, however, cut a far more measured figure when asked about allegations that a small group of selectors has run the process unchecked for years.
“I was surprised to hear that comment about bypassing the board. Hockey India can give a better answer to that”.

briefs.headline: Justice Mittal requests Delhi HC to implead AITA Trust and DLTA
briefs.bodyText:
The Delhi High Court-appointed administrator to the All India Tennis Association (AITA), Justice (retd.) Gita Mittal, has requested the Court to implead the AITA Trust and the Delhi Lawn Tennis Association (DLTA) in the ongoing proceedings to amend the AITA’s Constitution in line with the National Sports Governance Act and hold fresh elections.
In her report dated September 14, filed after the Extraordinary General Meeting ratified AITA’s new Constitution on July 26, Justice Mittal termed this as a necessary step under her Court-mandated “obligation to supervise the financial affairs of AITA” and because the AITA had “assigned and abdicated all its functions, properties and income to the AITA Trust”.
The administrator has stated that efforts to secure financial records have been unsuccessful so far, and has produced a letter written on June 30 by Anil Dhupar, secretary of AITA Trust, where he claimed that the Trust was an independent body and the request was beyond the scope of the Court’s mandate.
On July 25, The Hindu had highlighted the shifting of responsibilities from an elected, non-profit body like AITA to AITA Trust, the many conflicts of interests where the same officials occupied different positions across the AITA, AITA Trust and DLTA, and the wrangling between the AITA Trust and DLTA in mid-2025 over rental income worth nearly ₹40 crore from office spaces at the R.K. Khanna Stadium in Delhi.
Justice Mittal has stated that the rent dispute prima facie indicated “misappropriation of land and defalcation of funds, which were intended only for the interest of the game and have been surreptitiously diverted to private persons utilizing the shield of a legal entity in the nature of a Trust”.
The DLTA has been led for nearly a decade by Rohit Rajpal, India’s current Davis Cup captain and a vice-president at the AITA. He was the treasurer of the AITA Trust during the rent dispute, before resigning on June 13, 2026. Rajpal has since announced his candidature for AITA presidency, where tennis legend Leander Paes is expected to be a contender.
Fresh elections under the new Constitution were to be held by September 30, but the interim AITA committee has requested an extension. The High Court is scheduled to hear the matter again on September 25.
The International Tennis Federation (ITF) generally disapproves of ad-hoc bodies being in charge for extended periods. Emails from The Hindu requesting comment have received no response from the ITF.

briefs.headline: 'We're not machines, we're not robots, outside noise does affect us': Sanju Samson
briefs.deck: Sanju Samson recognizes the impact of public scrutiny on cricketers, yet he handles it with poise. In the second T20I against Afghanistan, he showcased his talent by scoring fifty-seven runs off just twenty-two balls. Rather than viewing his teammates as competitors for starting positions, he embraces their camaraderie. His experience as an IPL captain provides him with valuable insight into the…
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: 
Sanju Samson
 has spent years learning to live with the scrutiny that comes with playing for India. On Tuesday, after his 57 off 22 balls against Afghanistan in the second T20I, he admitted that the noise from outside does get through — even if his preferred response is to switch it off.
“I try to switch the Wi-Fi off. But sometimes the Wi-Fi gets switched on and comments become visible,” Samson said after India’s seven-wicket win. “Some senior player says something. So I think it’s very normal.”
Samson’s innings, in which 52 of his 57 runs came in boundaries, came at a time when his place at the top of India’s T20I order is under scrutiny. The emergence of 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has added another layer to the competition for the two opening slots alongside 
Abhishek Sharma
. Sooryavanshi had impressed on India’s recent tour of Zimbabwe, while Samson had been left out of that series after failing to convert his opportunities in the preceding Ireland, England series.
"Definitely, outside noise does affect cricketers in India,” Samson said. “But you need to be very clear about what your mindset is, how you need to prepare and what mindset you need to play with."
“I think I have been mature enough and experienced enough to know how to handle it. Earlier, it used to hurt a little. I’m not a machine. We are not robots that we can say, ‘No, it doesn’t affect me.’ Definitely, it affects you,” he said.
“If I paid attention to those things, I couldn’t bat like this,” Samson said. “Before hitting a shot, I would think ten times, ‘Yaar, out ho gaya toh phir Wi-Fi problem ho jayega.’ So instead, I tell myself, ‘Koi baat nahi.’”
That mindset has become particularly important as Samson finds himself competing for a place with a teenager who has rapidly forced his way into the conversation. Samson, however, said he does not view Sooryavanshi as a rival within the dressing room.
“I think they (Sooryavanshi and Abhishek Sharma) are competitors for the outside world, but we are a team and we are playing for a country,” he said. “We want to win the game first, and then it comes down to the other individuals.”
Samson also said his experience as an IPL captain has helped him understand why difficult selection calls have to be made. He acknowledged that the management has a difficult task in choosing between players who are all performing, while stressing that individuals have to remain ready for their opportunities rather than dwell on selection decisions.
“We can’t sulk or be in a negative frame of mind, thinking, ‘Yaar, mujhe nahi mila, usko kyun diya.’ Those kinds of mindsets don’t work here,” he said.
